statement: You are given a non-empty singly linked list whose node values, read from head to tail, are listed in values. Let n be the number of nodes.
The middle node is the one at 0-based position ⌊n / 2⌋. For an even n this is the second of the two central nodes. Delete it.
Return the resulting list, read from its head. A list with one node becomes empty.

examples.explanation: n = 5, so the node at position 2, holding 3, is removed.
n = 4, so the node at position 2, holding 9, is removed.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 10⁵]
